facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a 10-year history of pruritic lesions on the scrotum and buttock
pruritic lesions on the scrotum and buttock
He was previously treated at a local clinic with little improvement
He had no relevant medical history and no family history of similar skin problems
Scattered, well-defined, annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with an atrophic center and a slightly elevated edge on the scrotum, buttock, groin, and intergluteal cleft
There was no inguinal adenopathy
Routine blood work, including blood biochemistry, syphilis serologies, and HIV testing, were normal or negative

Revealed hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, parakeratotic columns (cornoid lamella) overlying dyskeratotic keratinocytes, and hypogranulosis with a perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis

hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, parakeratotic column (cornoid lamella), and several dyskeratotic keratinocytes in the epidermal invagination with hypogranulosis and perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
Clinical photograph showing scattered, well-defined, annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with an atrophic center with a slightly elevated edge on the scrotum, buttock, groin, and intergluteal cleft

Biopsy findings showing hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, parakeratotic column (cornoid lamella), and several dyskeratotic keratinocytes in the epidermal invagination with hypogranulosis and perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
Two specimens taken from the scrotum and buttock

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of scattered, well-defined, annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with an atrophic center and a slightly elevated edge, along with histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, and parakeratotic columns, is consistent with Darier disease.
The patient's symptoms of pruritic lesions on the scrotum and buttock, along with the presence of hyperkeratotic plaques, could be indicative of Grover disease.
The patient's presentation of well-defined, annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with an atrophic center and a slightly elevated edge is similar to that of psoriasis.
The patient's histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis and parakeratotic columns could be consistent with seborrheic keratosis.
The patient's symptoms of pruritic lesions on the scrotum and buttock, along with the presence of hyperkeratotic plaques, could be indicative of lichen planus.
The patient's histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis and parakeratotic columns could be consistent with squamous cell carcinoma.
The patient's histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis and parakeratotic columns could be consistent with basal cell carcinoma.
The patient's histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis and parakeratotic columns could be consistent with keratoacanthoma.
